metadata.title: What's Going On With AMD Stock Tuesday

content.text:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.
AMD (NASDAQ:AMD) shares fell about 7% in afternoon trading on Tuesday after the company entered a partnership with Core Scientific (NASDAQ:CORZ) to expand artificial intelligence infrastructure capacity.
The agreement will provide AMD access to more than 500 megawatts of data center capacity starting next year, with the collaboration potentially expanding to 2.5 gigawatts. The companies will work on infrastructure development and deployment of AMD Instinct GPUs, EPYC processors, and ROCm software.
Core Scientific shares climbed 10% following the announcement as investors reacted to the potential expansion of its AI-focused data center business.
Under the agreement, AMD will also receive market-priced warrants to purchase Core Scientific common stock, subject to specific conditions. The companies said the partnership is designed to support rising demand for AI computing from cloud providers, model developers, and enterprise customers.
